meta.regime: Two big regime shifts landed at once. (1) The FOMC held 9-3 at 3.50-3.75% - a sixth straight pause - but with three members dissenting FOR a hike and Warsh refusing any forward guidance, the market read it as a loss of anchor: 30-year yields spiked ~14bp to ~5.23% (a 19-year high), inflation expectations rose, the dollar slid and equities fell. Higher yields with a weaker dollar is a fiscal-dominance / stagflation tell, not a growth-friendly one. (2) The US-Iran pause has broken into open escalation: CENTCOM launched a heavy wave of strikes on Iran (Bandar Abbas and IRGC/maritime targets) after an intercepted Iranian attack, and Trump says it is the US turn to hit hard. WTI jumped ~6% to ~$84, the strait stays effectively closed, and the risk premium is re-armed and rising. Net regime: soft dollar, bid oil, bid havens (gold + franc), a real CAD terms-of-trade bid, and high-beta AUD pressured by risk-off. Gates today: BoE 11:00Z and US Q2 GDP 12:30Z; BoJ tomorrow.

dailyRead: The picture flipped overnight on two fronts. First, the Fed held 9-3 for a sixth straight meeting, but this was no soothing hold: three members (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) dissented in favour of a 25bp HIKE, and Chair Warsh pointedly refused to give any forward guidance. Markets hated the combination - 30-year Treasury yields ripped ~14bp to about 5.23%, a 19-year high, market inflation expectations rose, the dollar SLID and stocks fell (Dow -1.6%). Rising long yields alongside a falling dollar is a credibility/fiscal-dominance signal, and it is dollar-negative even though the hawkish dissents keep a September hike genuinely alive. Second, and bigger for the whole book, the US-Iran pause has collapsed into active fighting: CENTCOM launched a heavy wave of strikes on Iran (Bandar Abbas, IRGC and maritime targets) after intercepting an Iranian attack, and WTI surged about 6% to ~$84 with the Strait of Hormuz still choked to ~14 ships a day. That re-arms the risk premium and restores CAD's terms-of-trade bid, so USD/CAD flips from LONG to SHORT (soft dollar + firm oil). The cleanest expressions now: USOIL LONG (active escalation, but already +6% so size for a de-escalation snap-back); XAU/USD LONG (~$4,080, neared $4,100 on the slid dollar, higher inflation expectations and the haven bid) and XAG LONG alongside it; USD/CHF SHORT and USD/CAD SHORT on the soft dollar plus, respectively, a live haven bid and a real oil bid; EUR/USD LONG (dollar slide + the oil surge reviving the ECB September-hike energy case). Antipodeans: AUD/NZD SHORT still works - yesterday's soft AU Q2 trim (3.6% miss) deflated the RBA hike tail while NZD's 4.1% Q2 beat plus the oil surge REIGNITES its petrol-CPI engine - and AUD/CAD SHORT is now cleaner with CAD oil-bid. Yen: weakest by spot ~163.8, but the dollar slide and a thin-Friday MoF intervention threat cap the weakness into BoJ tomorrow, so USD/JPY is a short-tilt RANGE. Gates today: BoE 11:00Z (hold + MPR) and US Q2 GDP 12:30Z. The one caveat that caps the oil/haven longs: a single credible de-escalation headline snaps the premium back in a session.

geopolitics: The pause is over - this is active escalation, and oil is now one-way up on the risk premium. After an intercepted Iranian attack on US forces, CENTCOM launched a heavy wave of strikes on Iran, hitting Bandar Abbas (a southern port beside the strait) and dozens of IRGC command, missile, drone and maritime targets; Trump says it is the US turn to hit hard. WTI surged about 6% to ~$84 (Brent ~$89), and the Strait of Hormuz stays effectively closed - roughly 14 ships in the last 24 hours versus a pre-war ~120, with convoys under naval escort. FX transmission: (1) CAD gets a genuine terms-of-trade bid back - USD/CAD flips from LONG to SHORT (soft dollar + firm oil), though CAD is still domestically soft. (2) CHF's haven bid is live and directional, not marginal - USD/CHF SHORT, CHF the cleaner haven versus the energy-importing yen. (3) Gold and silver are bid on the slid dollar, higher inflation expectations and the haven flow (~$4,080 / ~$58) - XAU/XAG LONG. (4) The JPY loses ground as an oil importer but the dollar slide and MoF intervention risk cap its weakness - USD/JPY short-tilt RANGE. (5) High-beta AUD is the antipodean risk-off hurts most; NZD is cushioned because higher crude reignites its petrol-CPI engine. (6) USOIL flips to LONG. The single caveat that caps every oil/haven long: a credible de-escalation headline snaps the premium back in a session, so size for two-way headline risk even with the trend up.
